question.text: A plane is in level flight at a constant speed such that the speed of the air below the wings is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>144</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and above the wing is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If each of its wings has an area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, then the mass (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi></math>) of the plane is [<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ρ</mi><mi>air</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Given,

A=25 m2     [area of each wing]

v1=180×518 m s-1=50 m s-1     [speed of the air above the wing]

v2=144×518 m s-1=40 m s-1     [speed of the air below the wing]

According to Bernoulli's theorem

P1+12ρairv12=P2+12ρv22

⇒P2-P1=12ρairv12-v22

⇒P1-P2=12×1×502-402

⇒∆P=450 Pa

The lifting force acting on the plane is

∆P×Atotal=450×50 N=22500 N

Mg=∆P×Atotal

⇒M=2250 kg
